mechanism: Betamethasone may increase the risk of agranulocytosis and immunosuppression when combined with propylthiouracil, which independently carries agranulocytosis risk; additionally, corticosteroids can mask signs of infection and affect thyroid hormone metabolism.
action: Monitor complete blood count regularly, educate patient on signs of infection and agranulocytosis (fever, sore throat, unusual bleeding), and use lowest effective betamethasone dose with periodic reassessment.
